result.title: From Recursion to Convolution: Parallel Self-Improvement for Multi-Agent Systems
result.summary: Multi-agent self-improvement enables agents to improve through interaction and feedback. However, sequential dependencies across agents and refinement rounds can propagate errors, increase computational costs, and limit parallelism. Moreover, refining individual features or agents in isolation can overlook their dependencies and restrict collective coordination. To address these challenges, we propose ConvRSI, a framework for parallelizing multi-agent self-improvement through convolution. ConvRSI couples intra-agent convolution, which jointly refines related agent features, with inter-agent graph convolution, which aggregates messages according to the collaboration topology. Both stages operate in latent space, enabling parallel updates without repeatedly decoding and re-encoding intermediate messages. Experiments on MATH-500 show that ConvRSI achieves 5.04% performance improvement while reducing 17.27% inference cost, and 45.11% latency compared with RecursiveMAS. It also supports diverse collaboration patterns by representing their topologies as adjacency matrices. These results demonstrate the potential of convolutional co-evolution for efficient multi-agent self-improvement. Our code and datasets are provided in https://github.com/LYA2333/ConvRSI.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 ConvRSI，用「卷积」替代递归式多智能体自我改进：智能体内卷积联合精化相关特征，智能体间图卷积按协作拓扑聚合消息，两阶段均在 latent 空间完成，从而并行更新、避免反复解码重编码中间消息，在 MATH-500 上兼顾效果与推理成本、延迟。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本多智能体工作，无视觉成分；但其「在 latent 空间做并行状态更新并避免解码-重编码」的机制，可作为 LVR 中 parallel 生成与计算成本、长度权衡的借鉴线索，图卷积聚合也可能对应实体关系在内部状态中的传播，尚需核查。
